two-phase.label: Morgoth-depth pass leaves a stale skip entry
two-phase.explanation: At depth 100 the Borg first evaluates its special Morgoth-depth Teleport Other, which stores the same monster twice (Morgoth assumed present and little mana left). The regular Teleport Other evaluation then targets the kobold: the original also suppresses the hill giant left over in the second slot, valuing the cast at the kobold plus the giant instead of the kobold alone. The fix stops at the listed entries, so the value is one candidate's list.

no-morgoth-phase.label: Control: no deep pass, no phantom
no-morgoth-phase.explanation: Without the Morgoth-depth evaluation the second slot is never written. Both versions value the cast at the hill giant's danger, and the logs are identical before and after the fix.

single.label: Control: a stale self-entry is harmless
single.explanation: Only the kobold exists, so the deep pass stores the kobold in both slots. When the regular evaluation later reads one slot past its list, it finds the kobold itself: a duplicate, not a phantom. Both versions value the cast identically.
